series: Things Living In Your House, Part 10
sources: University of Kentucky Entomology, Clothes Moths (ENTFACT-609): adults do not feed and cause no injury to fabrics; adults lay about 40-50 eggs on vulnerable materials; worm-like larvae digest keratin, a fibrous protein in animal materials; larvae eat wool, fur, silk, feathers, felt and leather, plus lint and shed pet hair in vents and ducts; cotton and synthetics rarely attacked unless blended with wool or soiled with food stains or body oils; perspiration odors attract; avoid light, seldom seen; prefer dark closets, basements, attics; https://entomology.mgcafe.uky.edu/ef609

University of California IPM, Pest Notes: Clothes Moths (Publication 7435): larvae are the damaging stage; females lay 40-50 eggs; adults about 1/4 inch at rest; casemaking larvae carry a silken case that takes on the color of the fabric they eat; larval stage lasts 35 days to 2 1/2 years depending on temperature and food; adults are weak, fluttery flyers that stay near dark closets; laundering at 120 F or more for 20-30 minutes, or sealing in a bag and freezing for several days below 18 F, kills all stages; https://ipm.ucanr.edu/PMG/PESTNOTES/pn7435.html

NC State Extension, Clothes Moths and Carpet Beetles: Controlling Fabric Pests: fabric pests are among the few insects that can digest keratin; https://content.ces.ncsu.edu/clothes-moths-carpet-beetles-controlling-fabric-pests

title: The Moth in Your Closet Never Eats. Its Babies Eat Your Sweater 🧶
tiktok_caption: the moth in your closet never eats 🧶 its babies do, and they go for the sweaty clothes first. Would you check your wool sweaters tonight? 🔦 checking / 🙈 nope

beats.say: The moth in your closet never eats. Not once.
The clothes moth. Tiny, beige, and it hates the light.
The adult can't hurt your clothes. It just lays forty to fifty eggs.
Right on your wool sweater. In the dark.
Then the babies hatch, and start eating.
That hole in your sweater? That was dinner.
